evals.expected_output: The response reconstructs an evidence-backed C4 model, generates useful LikeC4 views, and validates edited LikeC4 files without presenting guesses as facts.
expectations: The response inspects executable, runtime, and deployment evidence before choosing boundaries.
Every modeled element and relationship has repository-relative implementation evidence.
Inferred facts and material unknowns are visibly distinguished from observed facts.
The response generates context, container, and selective component views rather than mirroring every file or class.
The response validates every edited LikeC4 source file, checks filteredErrors, and inspects rendered affected views or discloses why visual verification was unavailable.

evals.expected_output: The response models independently executable or deployable units as containers and keeps ordinary workspace libraries below the container level.
expectations: Container boundaries come from entrypoints, runtime commands, build outputs, or deployment configuration.
The response does not create a container solely because a workspace package or directory exists.
Runtime relationships require call-site or configuration evidence rather than dependency declarations alone.
The resulting container view remains focused and readable.

evals.expected_output: The response traces the requested flow through reachable implementation paths, records evidence, generates one dynamic view, and exposes any unresolved steps.
expectations: The response follows the flow from an entrypoint through handlers and outbound calls using source evidence.
The dynamic view contains only steps supported by the traced path and preserves parallel work rather than inventing a linear order.
Observed and inferred steps are distinguished in the evidence ledger.
Missing runtime wiring is reported as unknown rather than invented.
The generated LikeC4 source is validated and the rendered sequence view is inspected, or unavailable visual verification is disclosed.

evals.expected_output: The response compares existing LikeC4 definitions with implementation evidence, makes only necessary in-scope corrections, adds one focused view, validates it, and inspects its rendering.
expectations: The response finds the nearest LikeC4 project and preserves established identifiers, kinds, file organization, and view conventions.
Model drift is supported by implementation evidence and is corrected only when required for the requested truthful view; other drift is reported.
Current implementation and target architecture are not blended when intent is unclear.
The response uses full FQNs for cross-file references.
Every edited source validates with filteredErrors equal to zero, and unrelated totalErrors are reported separately.
Affected views are exported and visually inspected, or unavailable visual verification is disclosed.
